findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public service-provider interface, and adding `int order()` as an abstract method makes every existing third-party implementation binary-incompatible. An implementation compiled against the prior interface can still be discovered by ServiceLoader, but `detectProvider()` now invokes `order()` and will fail with AbstractMethodError; source consumers also cannot recompile without changes. Provide a default implementation (for example, a neutral/default priority) so existing providers remain usable.

findings.title: Equal-priority crypto providers are selected in nondeterministic ServiceLoader order
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider are all assigned order 200. When more than one of these providers is present, this code no longer rejects the invalid configuration as it did before; the stable sort preserves the unspecified ServiceLoader discovery order and silently uses whichever appears first. In particular, a deployment that includes both the default and FIPS providers can select the non-FIPS provider, defeating the expected FIPS crypto configuration. Retain rejection for tied highest-priority providers or assign an explicit, safe precedence.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns a non-Bouncy-Castle provider
findings.body: The CryptoProvider contract requires `getBouncyCastleProvider()` to return the Bouncy Castle security provider, but this implementation returns the provider backing the JVM's default keystore type. On standard JDKs that is commonly SUN/SUNJCE, not Bouncy Castle. Any code using the selected CryptoProvider to obtain the advertised BC provider can therefore receive an unrelated provider and fail when requesting BC algorithms or behavior. Since this provider intentionally has no BC dependency, it should not claim a default-keystore provider as Bouncy Castle; return an appropriate value/adjust the contract and callers, or implement the required provider behavior.
